Rashi on Megillah 12b:10:1.english: Carshena - Did they ever offer before You lambs of the first year?

Rashi on Megillah 12b:10:3.hebrew: מרס - שמירסו את הדם, שלא יקרש ושוב לא יהא ראוי לזריקה:
Rashi on Megillah 12b:10:3.english: Meres - [meaning] that they stirred the blood, so that it would not coagulate and then no longer be fit for sprinkling.

Rashi on Megillah 12b:10:4.hebrew: מרסנא - מירסו במנחות לבוללן; "ממרס" — לשון מגיס:
Rashi on Megillah 12b:10:4.english: Marsena - [They] stirred the meal-offerings to mix them; memares is an expression of magis [stirring].

Rashi on Megillah 12b:11:1.english: Prepared for calamity - [he] stands to be hanged.

Rashi on Megillah 12b:11:2.hebrew: מכאן שההדיוט קופץ בראש - שהרי מנה אותו הכתוב לבסוף, אלמא גרוע הוא מכולן, והוא קפץ בראש:
Rashi on Megillah 12b:11:2.english: From here [we see] that the common man jumps to the front - For Scripture listed him last; thus he was inferior to all of them, yet he jumped to the front.

Rashi on Megillah 12b:12:1.english: Were it not for the first letters - through which he [Ahasuerus] was regarded as a fool in the eyes of the nations:

Rashi on Megillah 12b:12:2.hebrew: לא נשתייר משונאי ישראל שריד ופליט - שהיו ממהרין להורגן במצות המלך באגרות האמצעיות, ולא היו ממתינים ליום המועד:
Rashi on Megillah 12b:12:2.english: There would not have been left among the enemies of the Jewish people a remnant or a refugee - for they would have hurried to kill them by the king's command in the middle letters, and they would not have waited for the appointed day:

Rashi on Megillah 12b:13:1.hebrew: אמרי מאי האי דשדר לן - אומרים האומות: מה זה ששלח לומר לנו "להיות כל איש שורר בביתו"? שאף הגרדן שורר בביתו:
Rashi on Megillah 12b:13:1.english: They say, "What is this that he has sent us?" - The nations say: What is this that he sent to tell us, "That every man should rule in his own house"? For even a weaver rules in his own house:

Rashi on Megillah 12b:15:1.hebrew: נערה - דוד לא ביקש אלא נערה אחת, כל אדם הראה לשלוחיו את בתו אולי תיטב בעיניו; ואחשורוש כסיל צוה לקבץ את כולן, הכל יודעין שלא יקח אלא אחת ואת כולן יבעל — מאן דהוה ליה ברתא מטמרה:
Rashi on Megillah 12b:15:1.english: A maiden - David sought only one maiden; every man showed his daughter to his emissaries, [thinking] perhaps she would find favor in his eyes. And Ahasuerus, [being] a fool, commanded to gather all of them; everyone knew that he would take only one and cohabit with all of them — [therefore,] whoever had a daughter hid her:

Rashi on Megillah 12b:18:1.hebrew: מוכתר בנימוסו היה - בשמות נאין, נימוס שם בלשון יון:
Rashi on Megillah 12b:18:1.english: [Mordecai] was crowned with his nimus - [That is,] with fine names; nimus [means] "name" in the Greek language:

Rashi on Megillah 12b:19:1.hebrew: (נערי) לא גרסינן, אלא הכי גרסינן: אמר רבה בר בר חנה אמר רבי יהושע בן לוי כו':
Rashi on Megillah 12b:19:1.english: We do not have the reading "(na'ari)"; rather, we read thus: "Rabbah bar bar Chanah said [that] Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said, etc.":

Rashi on Megillah 12b:19:2.english: Because David did not kill Shimei - for he was liable to the death penalty:

Rashi on Megillah 12b:1:1.hebrew: בוציני - דלועין קטנות, כלומר: דבאותו מין עצמו זה נואף וזו נואפת. הוא אומר להראות את יופיה, והיא לכך נתכונה שיסתכלו ביופיה:
Rashi on Megillah 12b:1:1.english: [With] botzinei - small gourds; that is to say, in the very same manner, he acts adulterously and she acts adulterously: he proposes to display her beauty, and she intended the same — that they would gaze at her beauty:

Rashi on Megillah 12b:20:1.hebrew: לאידך גיסא - לצעקה ולא לשבח: איש יהודי ואיש ימיני גרמו לי הצער הזה:
Rashi on Megillah 12b:20:1.english: From the opposite perspective - [She said this] as an outcry and not as praise: "A Judean man and a Benjamite man caused me this distress":

Rashi on Megillah 12b:5:2.hebrew: מלמד שפרחה בה צרעת - ויליף בירושלמי מ"אשר נגזר עליה", וכתיב: "וישב בית החפשית מצורע כי נגזר מבית ה'" (דברי הימים ב כו) — מה להלן צרעת, אף כאן צרעת:
Rashi on Megillah 12b:5:2.english: This teaches that she broke out in leprosy - And it is derived in the Jerusalem Talmud from [the verse], "[and] what was decreed [nigzar] against her" [Esther 2:1], and it is written: "And he dwelt in a house set apart [as] a leper, for he was cut off [nigzar] from the house of the Lord" (II Chronicles 26[:21]) — just as there [it refers to] leprosy, so too here [it refers to] leprosy:

Rashi on Megillah 12b:6:2.english: Drank wine against a thousand - Thus Scripture testified about him (Daniel 5:1):

Rashi on Megillah 12b:7:1.english: [His wine] will cease from him - his wine will abate a little from him.

Rashi on Megillah 12b:7:2.english: On its lees - On its sediment.

Rashi on Megillah 12b:8:1.hebrew: וטעמא אמרו ליה - ויפה אמרו לו, דודאי כן הוא, שמתוך שהאדם שקט, דעתו מיושבת עליו, שנאמר: "שאנן מואב מנעוריו ושוקט הוא אל שמריו", וסיפיה דקרא: "על כן עמד טעמו בו וריחו לא נמר":
Rashi on Megillah 12b:8:1.english: And they stated a reason to him - And they spoke well to him, for indeed it is so: since a person is at ease, his mind is settled, as it is stated: "Moab has been at ease from his youth, and he has settled on his lees," and the end of the verse [states]: "therefore his taste has remained in him, and his scent is not changed":

Rashi on Megillah 12b:9:1.hebrew: פסוק זה על קרבנות נאמר - "והקרוב אליו" — לשון הקרבת קרבן: מלאכי השרת הזכירו לפני הקב"ה את הקרבנות שהקריבו ישראל לפניו, לעשות להם נקמה בושתי, ותבא אסתר ותמלוך תחתיה:
Rashi on Megillah 12b:9:1.english: This verse is stated on account of offerings - "And those close to him [vehakarov elav]" is an expression of bringing an offering [hakravat korban]: the ministering angels mentioned before the Holy One, blessed be He, the offerings that Israel offered before Him, [asking Him] to take vengeance for them upon Vashti, and [that] Esther should come and reign in her place:

Tosafot on Megillah 12b:11:1.hebrew: ממוכן - יש מדרש שהיה דניאל, ולפי שהיה נשוי לשרית שהיתה גדולה ממנו, שלא היה יכול לכופה לדבר כלשונו, יעץ לעשות כן:
Tosafot on Megillah 12b:11:1.english: Memukhan - There is a Midrash that he was Daniel; and because he was married to a noblewoman who was greater than him [in status], [so] that he was unable to compel her to speak in his language, he advised [the king] to do so:

Tosafot on Megillah 12b:5:1.hebrew: שפרחה בה צרעת - בירושלמי מפרש דילפינן "נגזר" דכתיב גבי ושתי, מ"נגזר" דכתיב גבי עוזיה כשנצטרע, דכתיב ביה: "נגזר מבית ה'" (דברי הימים ב כ״ו:כ״א):
Tosafot on Megillah 12b:5:1.english: That she broke out in leprosy - In the Jerusalem Talmud, [it] explains that we derive [the word] "nigzar" ["was decreed"] that is written regarding Vashti from "nigzar" ["was cut off"] that is written regarding Uzziah when he became leprous, as it is written regarding him: "he was cut off [nigzar] from the house of the Lord" (II Chronicles 26:21):

Tosafot on Megillah 12b:7:1.hebrew: זיל לגבי עמון ומואב דיתבי בדוכתייהו כחמרא - וקשה, דהא פרק תפלת השחר (ברכות דף כח.) פריך: "וכי עמון במקומו יושב? והלא בא סנחריב ובלבלו!" לכך פר"ת דגרסינן הכא "מואב" לחוד, דקרא נמי לא הזכיר אלא מואב, דכתיב: "שאנן מואב". ובברכות נמי לא גרסינן אלא עמון, ומזה הטעם התירו ליהודה גר העמוני לבא בקהל; אבל משמע דגרי אינך לא רצו להתיר לבא בקהל, לפי שלא בלבל סנחריב מצרים ולא בלבל מואב. ומיהו קשה, דבברכות משמע באותה שהבאתי שסנחריב בלבל עמון, ובירמיה חשיב להו באותן שהגלה נבוכדנצר! וי"ל: לפי שסנחריב היה ראשון שבלבל, נקרא הכל על שמו, ועליו כתיב: "ואסיר גבולות עמים ועתידותיהם שוסתי"; אבל ודאי עיקר החורבן היה ע"י נבוכדנצר:
Tosafot on Megillah 12b:7:1.english: Go to Ammon and Moab, who have remained in their places like wine - And this is difficult, for in the chapter [entitled] Tefillat HaShachar (Berakhot 28a) [the Gemara] asks: "Does Ammon really dwell in its place? Did not Sennacherib come and mix it up!" Therefore, Rabbeinu Tam explained that here we read "Moab" alone, for the verse too mentioned only Moab, as it is written: "Moab has been at ease." And in Berakhot as well, we read only "Ammon," and for this reason they permitted Yehudah, the Ammonite convert, to enter the congregation; however, it is implied that the converts of the other [nations] they did not want to permit to enter the congregation, because Sennacherib did not mix Egypt and did not mix Moab. Nevertheless, it is difficult, for in Berakhot, in that [passage] which I cited, it is implied that Sennacherib mixed Ammon, whereas in Jeremiah [Scripture] counts them among those whom Nebuchadnezzar exiled! And one can answer: Since Sennacherib was the first who mixed [the nations], it is all called by his name, and regarding him it is written: "And I have removed the boundaries of peoples, and I have plundered their treasures"; however, certainly the main destruction was through Nebuchadnezzar:
